title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs): Treasury Repurchase Agreement Risk Management

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York / Treasury Market Practices Group

summary: The Treasury Market Practices Group (TMPG) issued best practice recommendations on May 22, 2025 for managing risk in the U.S. Treasury repo market, specifically calling for haircuts or margin on repo transactions to protect against counterparty credit, liquidity, and market risks. The guidance identifies systemic risks posed by inconsistent risk management practices in the non-centrally cleared bilateral repo market, where leverage may not be fully understood or properly priced by market participants.
key_points: TMPG recommends all Treasury repos be risk managed with haircuts or margin, in conjunction with other risk management tools such as position limits, netting agreements, and portfolio margining
Risks identified include lack of consistency/transparency in bilateral repo risk management and potential under-pricing of leverage in the system
Large quantities of repos without prudent risk management could pose systemic risks to overall market functioning if one or more participants default
Working group convened February 2023 included dealers, money funds, hedge funds, asset managers, FMUs, clearing banks, foreign central banks, Treasury Dept., and NY Fed staff
Recommended implementation deadline is June 2026, with firms prioritized by material counterparty exposures using a risk-based rolling approach
Centrally cleared repos already adhere to the best practice through CCP margining regimes, but a segment of non-centrally cleared bilateral repo market will remain outside central clearing
Legal documentation must describe margining regime including timing, frequency, thresholds, valuation, collateral, and close-out netting procedures
why_it_matters: This guidance addresses systemic vulnerabilities in the $1+ trillion Treasury repo market by promoting consistent margin and haircut practices across bilateral repo transactions. Poor risk management in this market contributed to the March 2020 repo market stress. With SEC-mandated central clearing expanding, the TMPG recognizes that not all repos will be eligible for CCP margining, making bilateral risk management best practices essential for market stability during stress periods.
market_structure_context: This document directly addresses Treasury repo market plumbing and risk management infrastructure. Key structural elements include: (1) distinction between centrally cleared repos (already compliant through CCP margin) vs. non-centrally cleared bilateral repos (primary focus of guidance); (2) emphasis on legally enforceable documentation for margining regimes; (3) recommendation for extended implementation (June 2026) to allow industry to adapt legal agreements alongside central clearing expansion; (4) cross-market participant working group approach to develop standards; (5) systemic risk concern around leverage opacity in bilateral repo market.
notes: Source is a high-quality policy guidance document from the NY Fed's TMPG. Published May 22, 2025 (within 90-day window). PDF format contained FAQs summarizing a white paper and best practice recommendations on Treasury repo risk management. Document is authoritative and directly relevant to market structure topics. Key focus is encouraging haircuts/margin on bilateral repo transactions to prevent systemic risk from counterparty defaults.
